transcript.text: AEG IKB64301FB induction hob keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off. Pan of pasta boiled over just before.

ER03 is not a code I can confirm for this exact AEG hob from the information available, so I would not attach a definite meaning to it. Given that it began immediately after pasta boiled over, the most likely cause is liquid or starchy residue across the touch controls: hobs beep and switch themselves off when they think a control is being held down. Isolate it at the cooker switch/fused spur, let it cool, then wipe the entire glass and control area with a barely damp cloth followed by a dry one; do not flood the edges. Leave it off for several hours to let any moisture dry, then try it again. If ER03 returns when the glass is completely clean and dry, moisture may have got under the control area or the control electronics may need an engineer.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
Yes there was starchy water across the slider. I'll wipe it dry and switch it off at the wall for a bit, then try again. A wooden spoon was also resting on the edge of the hob, I've moved it.

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. The spoon could have caused a touch-control warning, but with starchy water across the slider and the hob now beeping, displaying ER03 and shutting down, moisture contamination is the main concern. I still cannot confirm ER03’s exact meaning for this model, so it is safer to work from the symptoms rather than guess the code. Keep the hob isolated at the consumer unit/fuse box and do not use it again, even after wiping it, until a qualified appliance engineer has checked it. They will need to assess whether liquid has got beneath the glass into the touch-control or control electronics.

candidates: Liquid or residue on the touch-control area causing a false continuously-pressed key detection (high)
Moisture that has reached beneath the control area after the boil-over (medium)
